Plot a nested cross-validation result

Source: R/nested-results-plot.R
autoplot.nested_results.Rd

autoplot() draws one point per outer fold: the parameter values each fold selected, or each fold's score on the rows it held out.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nested_results'
autoplot(
  object,
  type = c("parameters", "performance"),
  metric = NULL,
  eval_time = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A nested_results from nested_tune_grid() or a related function.

type

Which view to draw: "parameters" (the default) or "performance".

metric, eval_time

For type = "performance", the metrics and the evaluation times to draw. NULL, the default, draws them all. A metric that does not depend on time is drawn whatever eval_time names, as in tune's autoplot().

...

Not used, and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The outer folds run along the x axis in design order. With type = "parameters", each panel shows one tuned parameter, and the y axis is the value each fold selected. A flat row of points means the folds agreed. Points at different heights mean the tuning procedure picks different values on different data, which the averaged metrics hide.

With type = "performance", each panel shows one metric, and the y axis is each fold's score. A line marks the nested estimate that collect_metrics() reports.

A failed fold keeps its place on the x axis and draws no point. A panel label such as rmse (from 2 folds) shows that some completed folds gave no value there, such as an NA score. If no fold completed, the function gives an error. A run with no tuned parameters, such as a nested_fit_resamples() result, can only be drawn with type = "performance".

See also

nested_tune_grid(), print.nested_results(), collect_metrics(), summary.nested_results_set() for the same two views of a workflow-set run

Examples

data(mtcars)

rec <- recipes::recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) |>
  recipes::step_pca(recipes::all_predictors(), num_comp = tune::tune())
wf <- workflows::workflow(rec, parsnip::linear_reg())

set.seed(1)
folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2),
  inside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2)
)
set.seed(2)
res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:2))
autoplot(res)

autoplot(res, type = "performance")

autoplot(res, type = "performance", metric = "rmse")
